summary:
PASS 1 grind (2026-08-04): Settings went from nav-only (15 of 17 visible pages showing only the generic placeholder) to fully built. Header chrome (gear icon + 'Settings' title, prose font) now matches; the CONNECTION/AGENTS/TELEMETRY/APP rail groups render (MasterDetail gained group-header support). Every backed page now renders real content sourced from actual GET calls (providers/models/commands/prompts/agentBlueprints/expertPacks/mcpServers/hooks/policies/memoryStats/metrics/health/capabilities) or genuine client state (the connection registry, wire/plugins.ts, wire/settings-export.ts, theme.ts preferences) -- Settings.tsx now takes a real `client` prop threaded from SessionView instead of rendering with none. Plugins and Data & backups were reclassified from 'unbacked' to 'client': both had complete, working modules (wire/plugins.ts, wire/settings-export.ts) that were simply never wired to a nav entry -- that was a stale claim, not a real gap. The 'Agents' nav item's true backing was corrected from client.agents() (the expert/agent-blueprint CATALOG -- confirmed wrong by SessionView's own comment distinguishing it from 'connected clio deployments') to the same live-connection data Backends uses. Only Relays remains genuinely unbacked (ships hidden, per #337's established pattern) -- no relay registry route exists on either side. Several pages honestly diverge from a literal prototype-text copy where doing otherwise would misrepresent a real, working backend (Memory would have to claim a live cache subsystem 'reports no memory capability'; Models' 'router lm' role does not exist in the wire) -- those are called out per-item below and are NOT silently omitted.

PASS 2 grind (2026-08-05): re-verified every non-'match' item against the current tree. Two real fixes landed: (1) the independent audit's Prose-font downgrade (raw union keys rendered as button labels) is fixed -- added PROSE_FONT_LABELS + per-button font-face preview, locked by a new failing-first test, now 'match'. (2) The tree moved since PASS 1: clio-agent#1179 (the same backend gap the rail footer's 'relay unknown' indicator cites) landed GET /v1/relay/status. Added Client.relayStatus() to @clio/core and built RelaysPage.tsx -- Relays is no longer hidden; it renders the ONE real configured relay (reachable/detail from a live TCP probe) with the registry-management gap (add/remove, multi-host, per-host latency) visibly degraded rather than silently unavailable. The remaining 'deviates' items (Backends, Providers, Models, Agents, Policies, Memory, Metrics, Agent blueprints) were re-read against the current source and re-verified live via fresh side-by-side composites -- all already use the same real-data-plus-visible-degradation pattern correctly and no further fix was possible without a backend route that does not exist; their status and reasoning stand unchanged as accurate 'deviates', not stale claims.

PASS 3 grind (2026-08-05): re-verified every non-'match' item against the current tree; PASS 2's 'no further fix possible' call was wrong for three of them -- the tree hadn't moved, but the reads had missed real data SessionView already held. (1) Metrics: PASS 2's own fix_hint named the exact fix -- prop-drilled SessionView's already-computed real per-session numbers (a `tool_call`-part transcript count matching Observability's own `obsToolCount`, the pill's raw `SessionAgentTask[]` rows, and the context state's raw token/limit numbers) straight into Settings instead of substituting unrelated global counters. MetricsPage now renders the prototype's literal 4-row set, all real, all session-scoped -- 'match'. (2) Policies: the 'default approval mode' row was reading a `default_approval_mode` field that has NEVER existed on GET /v1/policies (confirmed by reading permission_policies.py's validator in full -- the route only ever returns a flat rule list) -- a dead code path, not a deliberate read-only choice. The prototype's own subtitle names the REAL source ('the composer approval toggle') -- the active session's real `approval_mode`, threaded down the same way and writable via the same `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}` Composer already uses. 'Ask' now reads and writes for real (the one safe, unambiguous direction); 'Execute' reads real state honestly but stays a documented degraded control rather than guessing among 3 real non-ask modes -- still 'deviates', but no longer a permanently-dead row. (3) Agent blueprints: re-read the prototype's OWN markup precisely and found only ONE row (the active session's own blueprint) templates a count at all -- the other two rows are freeform per-blueprint prose in the mock itself, not a formula. Threaded the real active-session blueprint id through to make ONE extra detail fetch (not N+1) and derive a real 'N declared children' count from that blueprint's own `agents` array -- still 'deviates' (no file-count concept exists anywhere on the wire), but the children count is now real. Backends/Providers/Models/Agents/Relays/Memory were re-verified against the current clio-agent tree (routes read in full) and confirmed genuinely unchanged -- their 'deviates' status and reasoning stand. All fixes locked by new tests/unit/settings.test.tsx cases (18 total now) and verified live via fresh side-by-side composites; full suite green (512 tests), build green, lint clean (pre-existing unrelated issues only).

items.app_evidence: PASS 3 fix (2026-08-05): the PASS 1/2 read was WRONG about where this row's data comes from, not just about writing it. GET /v1/policies (clio_agent.gact.routes.permissions.list_policies) has never carried a `default_approval_mode` field -- it always returns a flat list of {scope, action, kind, ...} rules (clio_agent.gact.runtime.permission_policies._validate_permission_policies) -- so the prior `readApprovalMode(doc)` always returned null against a real backend; the row was permanently blank/unchecked, a dead code path disguised as 'deliberately read-only'. The prototype's OWN subtitle names the real source correctly: 'The composer approval toggle sets the per-session default' -- the ACTIVE SESSION's real `approval_mode`, the exact value/setter (`detail.approval_mode` / `client.patchSession(id, {approval_mode})`) Composer's own approval picker already reads and writes, now threaded through SessionView -> Settings -> PoliciesPage. The real approval_mode is clio's actual 4-way enum (ask/auto-edits/bypass/ai-review), not the prototype mock's binary ask/execute: 'Ask' reflects+writes `approvalMode === 'ask'` for real (PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}, always the safe direction regardless of which mode was active); 'Execute' honestly reflects the real non-ask state (checked whenever the session is in ANY of the other 3 modes) but does not write -- there is no single unambiguous target among auto-edits/bypass/ai-review to pick on the user's behalf, so that stays a documented DegradedButton-style disabled control with the real current mode named in its title, not a silent guess (e.g. defaulting to 'bypass', which would silently strip more safety review than the user asked for). Allow rules stay real (raw JSON rows or the exact empty-state copy). Locked by tests/unit/settings.test.tsx ("reflects the active session's real approval mode..." + "shows an honest disabled Policies approval-mode row with no active session"). Verified live: screenshots/side-by-side/settings-policies.png -- the demo session's real mode is 'ask', rendering 'Ask ✓' cyan-selected exactly as the prototype's own mock does.
items.backend_surface: GET /v1/policies (real, allow rules) + PATCH /v1/sessions/{id} approval_mode (real, the SAME write the composer's own picker makes) -- corrected from the wrong /v1/policies-document claim; PUT /v1/policies itself remains unwired (whole-document replace, out of scope here)
